notes.details: Keep prompt definitions and trigger priority in ContextualCombatTutorial, keep presentation in ContextualCombatPrompt, and integrate RunScene only through combat context plus interaction completion hooks. Prompt state persists under combat_micro_prompt_states; the layout host belongs above the hand so prompts never cover board targets or HUD anchors.

notes.summary: Pre-battle Active Deck uses counted dense tiles at supported sizes
notes.details: The committed pre-battle overlay groups duplicate card ids into xN tiles and switches to the 120px three-column dense layout at nine groups (attuned magic is always dense). This keeps the 19-card maximum immediately visible without a deck scrollbar at 1280x720 and larger; retain the auto ScrollContainer only for genuinely extreme overflow.

notes.summary: Command buttons use scalable UiSkin variants, not state bitmaps
notes.details: Player-facing command/action Buttons and OptionButtons should use UiSkin compact, standard, large, destructive, selected, or icon StyleBoxFlat variants plus the non-interactive themed ornament. Do not reintroduce stretched per-state bitmap buttons. Card widgets and parchment navigation lists are intentional non-command exceptions. Styling must preserve existing focus modes, neighbors, controller traversal, and bindings.

notes.summary: Mid-enemy saves require snapshot continuations
notes.details: A pass or enemy-action checkpoint is not resumable merely because its dictionary is coherent: empty/transition and enemy actors cannot accept player input, and replaying CombatEngine would duplicate actions, counters, status ticks, or RNG. Persist a bounded pending_combat_checkpoints cursor of already-resolved full combat snapshots, consume/save those snapshots in order after load, and retain an explicit transition actor so legacy saves that omit current_actor can still default safely to a player turn.

notes.summary: Record run results through the supplied terminal state before persistence
notes.details: Terminal commit paths must pass their terminal dictionary through this state-in/state-out helper, adopt the embedded progression before ember banking/loss and save_data, and only then set processed flags. The bounded completed-result ledger preserves the original stats and NEW BEST decision for non-adjacent replay; UI-only victory/defeat hooks are not a durable save boundary.

notes.summary: Combat card alternatives use an exclusive mode selector
notes.details: A clicked card immediately enters its printed action. PRINTED, ATTACK 20, and MOVE 2 must be presented as one mutually exclusive radio-style mode selector, not navigation tabs: exactly one selected option uses a filled indicator and strong fill; available unselected options stay bright; unavailable options are substantially dimmed and desaturated. Keep the live fallback values visible and do not squeeze neighboring labels to fit.

notes.summary: Combat preview caches are revision-scoped and semantics-tested
notes.details: Card previews/options, shortcut plans, and pass forecasts cache only within an unchanged combat-state/selection revision; state replacement and selection progression must call the corresponding mark/invalidate helper. Direct test-state assignment is covered by state hashes. Optimized move legality, AOE target lookup, movement plans, and shortcut prefilters retain exhaustive-reference equality checks in the performance harnesses.

notes.summary: CombatBoardView uses read-only borrowed snapshots and retained static rendering
notes.details: RunScene may pass combat/presentation dictionaries by reference because CombatBoardView never mutates them. The view keeps a deep snapshot only of derived-cache inputs to detect later in-place changes, indexes per-tile render data, lazily loads only submitted unit types, and renders invariant background/floors on the parent while its internal dynamic layer handles previews, units, particles, and animation. Preserve the static/dynamic draw-order equivalence and mutation-detection tests when changing submissions.

notes.summary: Pooled card proxy widgets must clear stretch anchors after configure
notes.details: A reused CardWidget child under CardProxy can silently double from 250x352 to 500x704 when FULL_RECT anchors resolve again during configure, even while the proxy scale itself reports the correct value. Keep the CardWidget at fixed native top-left geometry, reapply _prepare_native_card_widget after configure/display overrides, and let the proxy parent own all drag/play/draw/discard scaling. Visual probes should assert the child widget size across multiple pool reuse cycles, not only the proxy scale.

notes.summary: Card motion should be continuous, brief, and action-first
notes.details: A played card should use one persistent proxy, grow modestly into center for only a short identification beat, then complete its shrink-and-pile flight before any card action animation starts so it never covers movement, damage, block, or other resolution visuals. Keep the full pre-action cadence quick. Multi-card draws should remain smooth and overlapping but launch as a readable stream with enough stagger to perceive one card, then the next, rather than appearing simultaneous.

notes.summary: Combat log should be prominent and own missed-gear copy
notes.details: Keep the combat log as a larger high-contrast framed panel with body-large outlined text; missed-equipment disintegration copy belongs only in the combat log, not the action banner.

notes.summary: Loadout discovery uses separate navigation and per-asset states
notes.details: Acquired equipment, consumable items, and magic ids are recorded in both unread_loadout_* for the top-bar/tab notification and new_loadout_* for item-level NEW tags. Opening Gear or Magic clears only its navigation unread list; hovering the specific asset clears and persists only that asset's NEW state, so the panel can guide the eye after its tab badge has already been acknowledged.

notes.summary: Flurry repeats effects but pays Time once
notes.details: Cards with top-level flurry:true snapshot all currently available card plays, expand their printed actions once per snapped play, multiply health cost per copy, discard one physical card, and pay the top-level Time cost only once. The commit spends the snapshotted plays; bonuses or kill refunds created during resolution remain afterward. Fallback Attack/Move modes do not inherit Flurry.

notes.summary: Flurry cards should be modest per copy but premium in total
notes.details: Do not overcorrect Flurry by making each printed package anemic. Keep each repeat below the rate of a normal standalone card, but tune the baseline two-copy result into the premium build-around band; the July 2026 midpoint pass landed the five payoffs around 4.6-5.7. Card-play enablers may be strong enough to make the setup exciting, including Gathering Rhythm granting 2 plays.

notes.summary: Umbra hiding must cover every player-facing information surface
notes.details: Filtering only enemy sprites is insufficient. Hidden enemies must also be removed from direct targets and threat previews; anonymized in initiative, logs, intent/action animation banners, pass-risk forecasts, and floating combat text; and ignored during movement planning until collision. Preserve visible outcomes without leaking hidden identity, position, intent, or damage forecasts.

notes.summary: Radiance effects share activation-based Umbra duration semantics
notes.details: Illuminate creates ranged circular light sources, Vision extends the player's Manhattan radius, Truesight reveals enemies without lighting tiles, and Dispel reduces the effective stage. Duration -1 is persistent; positive durations tick on the player's next activation.

notes.summary: Umbra discovery must occur only after an irreversible choice
notes.details: Speculative hover, risk, shortcut, and continuation previews must never resolve hidden collision or visibility. If a multi-step movement card reveals new Umbra information after click, lock cancellation and card switching until its remaining actions resolve or are skipped; Illuminate-and-attack cards reuse the clicked light target and commit without a second cancellable reveal step.

notes.summary: Render Umbra behind board objects and label it separately from elemental intensity
notes.details: Umbra should shade the board atmosphere while character sprites, props, and equipment pickups remain crisp in the foreground. Present its stage as a dedicated room-header line such as 'Deep Umbra'; the elemental intensity HUD remains five elements only.

notes.summary: Umbra effects must remain legible during combat
notes.details: Active temporary light sources need persistent on-board markers with duration counters; True Sight needs a player-HUD badge, counter, and tooltip; expired light should let fog visibly creep back over about one second; and Umbra action icons should favor bold small-size silhouettes over detailed art.

notes.summary: Combat notes stay fixed while the board moves
notes.details: Board zoom and pan must not trigger contextual combat prompt relayout. The note is fixed HUD information; navigation_changed should remain a board signal but should not be connected to prompt placement.

notes.summary: Combat board renders on a HUD underlay canvas
notes.details: The navigable board must remain unclipped so its art can flow beneath the bottom controls. Keep the board and base backdrop in BoardUnderlay below UiLayer, align the board's interactive rect to StageRoot, and leave broad UI layout controls mouse-filtered to IGNORE so input still reaches the board.

notes.summary: Flurry uses a wide timeline icon with a shallow card-row slot
notes.details: The approved direction is a 112x64 transparent timeline: two crimson outline card echoes progress along a gold baseline into one fully rendered parchment card. CardWidget gives the Flurry token about 1.8x normal width but only 1.05x normal height; doubling a square slot made the following row gaps visibly too large. Keep it distinct from Draw's upright stacked-card silhouette and validate at native 250x352 card size.

notes.summary: Introduce Fringe Umbra before the first elemental dragon
notes.details: Keep depth 1 Clear, then use Fringe on first-section depths 2 and 3 and retain Fringe for the depth-4 boss. Later section stages remain Fringe, Advancing, Pressing, Deep, and Heart rather than shifting the entire curve forward. The card heuristic uses 0.75 Umbra relevance because only the first depth is guaranteed Clear.

notes.summary: Radiance does not determine Grimoire card provenance
notes.details: Radiance cards unlock the shared Radiance/effect articles, but their card pages follow their source taxonomy. Reward or attuned Radiance cards use Magicks; equipment-only Radiance cards such as Lantern Shot receive a card-preview entry under the granting equipment slot instead of being mislabeled as Magicks.

notes.summary: One card action line represents one target selection
notes.details: When multiple card actions use reuse_previous_target, render their icons on the same logical and physical line because a new line communicates a new target choice. Keep automatic non-target effects on their own rows as needed, and avoid wrapping a shared-target row into apparent extra target lines. Matching range tokens within the shared target group should be shown once.

notes.summary: Hidden RunScene probes must also hide nested CanvasLayers
notes.details: Setting the RunScene root Control invisible does not suppress children moved under BoardUnderlay or UiLayer CanvasLayers. Isolated card-art probes that instantiate RunScene for helper methods must explicitly hide nested CanvasLayer nodes, or startup UI can cover the proof while image-dimension checks still pass.

notes.summary: Umbra should read as filled, billowing tile shadow
notes.details: Keep every concealed tile clearly darkened for tactical readability, then layer coherent rounded violet-black cloud lobes with visible slow drift. Boundary contours should stay thin and subordinate; avoid long narrow ribbons or zig-zag bands that make the effect look like linework.

notes.summary: Merchant trade overlay must size its host to real content
notes.details: Merchant panel content is taller than the generic 248px relic-choice host; centering oversized content can clip the panel bottom at 1280x720 and leave it unsafe near laptop/full-HD viewport edges. Size the host from _relic_choice_bar.get_combined_minimum_size().y, keep the merchant control labeled Hide with Return to Shop and Escape as reversible access, and cover fresh 720p and 1080p launches in merchant_room_probe.

notes.summary: Card action context stays compact, card-anchored, and motion-stable
notes.details: For normal card targeting and the Printed/Attack/Move choice, omit action-type and target-validity/turn-end-risk rows. Position the contextual widget directly above the active hand card. When play commits, lock the widget's exact screen position through card-flight and action-resolution animations so hand rebuilding or reflow cannot shift it; retain drag-only release guidance.

notes.summary: Pause and settings scrim must use an absolute top gameplay z-order
notes.details: RunScene combat HUDs, fanned hand cards, and transient effects use positive or absolute z-index values up to the 1600s. A modal scrim left at z=0 will dim only lower siblings while cards and turn/pass widgets render over it. Keep MenuScrim z_as_relative=false above gameplay surfaces; both the pause dialog and in-run SettingsPanel stay descendants of that scrim.

notes.summary: Terrain destruction presentation is transition-driven
notes.details: Zero-HP terrain is hidden by normal board drawing, so RunScene diffs before/after terrain state, holds destruction frame 0 during impact/floating-text presentation, then supplies presentation-only terrain_destruction_units through the animation. Tile-scoped damage sources such as player/enemy AOE, deterministic lightning strikes, and trap blasts should apply the same damage to destructible terrain on every affected tile.

notes.summary: Enemy activations share one deterministic plan across resolution, preview, animation, and analytics.
notes.details: Targeted move-plus-attack intents minimize movement to an attack-enabling endpoint first, then prefer safer equal-length paths; move-away attacks preserve the attack, while attackless retreats maximize safe separation. Future routing uses finite terrain-clearing and trap costs, treats allies as hard current but temporary future blockers, and credits an immediately traversable prefix to avoid needless stalls. Exact hover projections reuse the plan and honor freeze, shock, immobilize, and deterministic lightning tiles.

notes.summary: Enemy ember gains should be quiet, brief, and header-local
notes.details: On enemy death, do not play the ember-collect sample or launch board-traveling currency motes. Combine simultaneous kill rewards into one exact counter gain, roll the header count in about 0.2 seconds, and limit flair to a restrained warm pulse plus a terse +N beside the counter; reduced-motion should remain supported.

notes.summary: Character Gear loadout must scroll inside the fixed body
notes.details: The five gear slots plus item slots exceed the fixed character body at supported viewports. Leaving that column unscrolled raises the shared HBox minimum height, so every Gear subpanel extends beneath CharacterBodyFrame and is clipped. Keep the outer dialog/tab bounds fixed and contain the loadout list in its own vertical ScrollContainer.

notes.summary: Movement paths use slim dimensional unified arrows with shared cyan/purple geometry
notes.details: Keep the seamless isometric silhouette, translucent gradient, outline, and shadow. Current approved direction uses shaft ratio 0.333, head width 0.405, tip reach 0.138, and tail reach 0.285; player paths are cyan, enemy intent/move paths are purple, ground items stay below the path, and units/floating equipment stay above it.

notes.summary: MSAA visual probes require an automatic GPU-backed renderer
notes.details: The game enables project-wide 4x 2D MSAA. Godot's --headless dummy renderer cannot render or validate MSAA, so visual_probe_runner reads project.godot and automatically selects a native display renderer when MSAA is enabled (Metal/Mobile on macOS), or emits a clear capability error when no display is available. Non-MSAA projects retain the previous headless default.

notes.summary: Pre-battle enemy frames use complete static combat art
notes.details: Turn-order portraits are intentionally tighter crops and can omit parts of enemies (notably Zekarion). Pre-battle summary/detail frames should prefer each enemy art_path with keep-aspect-centered fitting; turn-order UI keeps its separate portrait mapping.

notes.summary: Cursor feedback classifies real activation separately from hover help
notes.details: CURSOR_HELP is informational and produces dull click feedback. Point-dependent actions expose cursor_feedback_context_at(local_position); dynamically guarded Controls use cursor_feedback_context_provider with guards matching their real input handlers. Static targets may use cursor_feedback_context and cursor_feedback_drag_source. CursorFeedback owns exact-once procedural click sounds and scene-transition loading feedback.

notes.summary: Custom cursor reacts through its forged body without press-only ornament
notes.details: Keep one coherent forged silhouette with broad blade facets, housed pommel bearing, held compression, release rebound, and directional drag deformation. A valid press must not introduce a detached white tip glint, sparkle, glyph, or other overlay; motion and material changes provide the feedback. Loading alone may use a single sweep inside the bearing.

notes.summary: Modal hit tests must use one canvas coordinate space
notes.details: RunScene native macOS mouse events already match Control.get_global_rect() canvas coordinates. Do not also compare Viewport.get_final_transform() * event.position in production: that creates an inverse-transformed second live hit region where unrelated clicks can close the modal. Tests and replay that synthesize canvas coordinates should route them with Viewport.push_input(event, true).

notes.summary: Modal cursor feedback must mirror suppressed input
notes.details: When a focused pre-battle enemy inspection is open, the full-screen pinned-tooltip scrim consumes every background click without dismissal. Its cursor_feedback_context_provider must therefore return action only over the live X close-button rect and inert everywhere else; retaining the generic pinned-overlay outside-click action context produces a valid cursor/click sound for an action that will never occur.

notes.summary: Escape the Umbra Steam trailer uses deterministic current-game capture and Remotion source
notes.details: Editable source lives in marketing/trailer; tools/steam_trailer_capture.gd produces route, prebattle, real CombatEngine trap/AoE/Umbra beats, and reward footage. The shadow-dragon main-menu art is narrative goal imagery only, and the retired teaser is not a creative reference.

notes.summary: Targetless card clicks require card-anchored confirmation
notes.details: Clicking a playable card may arm and preview its Printed mode, but a card whose preview completes without a board target must not resolve until the highlighted Play Card action in the compact card-anchored rail is pressed. Keep Printed/Attack/Move switchable before commitment; Cancel or selecting another card must not spend, resolve, or emit card-play analytics. Drag-to-board remains confirmed by its explicit drop.

notes.summary: Pre-render Labyrinth Crumble trailer copy instead of loading the TTF at Remotion runtime
notes.details: Chromium FontFace.load() intermittently left @remotion/fonts delayRender handles open during long renders, including with TTF, compact WOFF, embedded data URLs, and single-worker rendering. scripts/render-title-cards.py deterministically rasterizes the finite promo copy from fonts/LabyrinthCrumble-Regular.ttf into transparent PNGs; animate those assets in Remotion and regenerate them when copy or typography changes.

notes.summary: Do not await Tween.finished after independent timer awaits unless the tween is still running.
notes.details: At fixed frame rates, the ember counter's frame-quantized roll timers can outlast its pulse tween. Connecting to finished after it already fired suspends the coroutine forever and leaves RunScene's card-resolution animation lock set. Guard late awaits with is_valid() and is_running().

notes.summary: Audit deferred Godot trailer UI frame-by-frame before choosing source trims
notes.details: A correct non-start RunEngine state does not guarantee the first visible Movie Maker frames are safe: large-map and prebattle overlays can draw several frames after their state-changing calls complete, briefly exposing the underlying room or a half-composed overlay. Keep the RunScene hidden while preparing the requested UI, physically trim each edit source past its measured stable frame, and verify a dense early-frame contact sheet plus every encoded transition. For the deterministic route/prebattle captures, capture-footage.sh currently uses raw-frame trims 27 and 56.

notes.summary: Board equipment pickups reuse the RunScene equipment tooltip builder
notes.details: CombatBoardView emits equipment:<id> tooltip triggers and calls an injected equipment_tooltip_builder. RunScene wires _build_equipment_tooltip_panel in _ready so collectible equipment shows the same supplied-card previews as the equip menu while the board remains reusable; without a builder, the board falls back to a framed name-and-slot tooltip.

notes.summary: Trailer tactical footage must preserve authentic generated rooms and production card play
notes.details: For Escape the Umbra trailers, capture a real non-start engine-generated room with its walls, props, moss, loot, enemies, and legal run state. Drive cards through the production hand selection, targeting, center-stage card, discard, and resolution flow; compose camera motion around that footage instead of direct action-step shortcuts or synthetic empty grids. Light-source shots must visibly and mechanically clear real Umbra darkness, with before/after visibility assertions.

notes.summary: Trailer camera uses continuous action-timed phases
notes.details: For UI choices, use one eased approach into the real option area, an intentional readable hold, a selection-timed impact, and one eased pullback. Do not apply Bezier easing separately across multi-waypoint interpolation tracks because it visibly stops and restarts. Keep the lower source edge covered, remove shading over action UI, and spend added pacing before the actual selection rather than on an empty post-choice room. Validate composed motion at dense frame cadence.

notes.summary: Unconfirmed movement previews must preserve committed Umbra information
notes.details: Card simulations may internally move the player, change vision or Umbra, collide with concealed enemies, and trigger traps or loot. Until the card crosses the existing irreversible commit boundary, render the committed player, Umbra, traps, loot, log, and visibility while retaining safe preview data such as damage to already-visible enemies; otherwise previews disclose hidden board state before Play Card confirmation.

notes.summary: Reward capture must move CanvasLayer UI inside its own viewport
notes.details: RunScene board and reward UI live in CanvasLayers, so scaling the parent Control does not affect recorded pixels. For trailer relic and spell captures, mount the production RunScene in a larger 16:9 SubViewport, position the production choice host before it becomes visible, assert the selected control clears the viewport bottom safety margin, and inspect the encoded source frame before compositing.

notes.summary: Trailer menu cameras follow the real swap once
notes.details: For Magic and Equipment loadout footage, use one restrained approach zoom, one continuous source-to-destination follow aligned to the real drag or swap, a short result hold, and one pullback. Do not use multi-waypoint pan and scale tracks that change direction or apply eased motion separately per segment. Validate at dense frame cadence.

notes.summary: Dragon bosses use seeded gates; Noctyrax closes the run with visibility-focused adds
notes.details: DragonBossLibrary deterministically shuffles Tharokh, Vyraketh, Vaeloryx, Iskaldra, and Zekarion across depths 4/8/12/16/20 without repeats; Noctyrax is fixed at depth 24 and enters with two depth-scaled Veilbound Acolytes. Boss-bar actors remain revealed through Umbra. Large enemies use the established red attack glow and pulsing boundary across their full footprint when any visible footprint tile is a legal direct target; all footprint tiles click the same actor. Boss name, exact HP, segmented health, and damage preview live entirely inside a boss dossier that replaces the TURN CLOCK legend column without increasing the turn-order panel height or covering the board. Boss encounters end when the boss-bar actor dies even if authored hazards or adds remain.

notes.summary: Elemental intensity is a contested room resource with centralized scaling rules
notes.details: Player cards with top-level intensity_cost synthesize one required spend before printed actions; enemy actions build with type:intensity or pay attached spend_intensity costs. Trap damage is centralized in scripts/elemental_intensity_rules.gd at 72/94/124/162/208/262/324 percent for intensity 0-6, and generated traps preserve base_damage with damage fallback for older saves.

notes.summary: Placed light uses soft animated glow without construction lines
notes.details: Placed light must preserve the exact Illuminate Manhattan gameplay footprint while presenting it as overlapping blurred warm falloff with no hard tile or perimeter outline. The orb should use a feathered luminous core, close glow, gentle breathing scale/brightness, subtle bob and internal drift, while keeping the remaining-activation text readable without a framed badge.

notes.summary: Funded intensity spenders reuse the gated-card glow
notes.details: Do not add a separate bracket, corner, notch, or inward-siphon frame around intensity-spending cards; the user considers that ornament crude and unpolished. A spender whose cost is currently payable should use the existing elemental IntensityActiveGlow exactly like a satisfied intensity gate, while an unpayable spender stays unlit. Keep the negative elemental amount in the cost row as the distinction between spending and gating.

notes.summary: Card scoring uses a fixed-initiative no-skill reference profile
notes.details: Player base initiative is fixed at 9. Qualitative progression effects stay outside intrinsic printed-card coefficients; use the progression_skills analytics context to compare learned-skill cohorts and note exceptional interactions during review.

notes.summary: Stone floor variants use isolated tile-only textures
notes.details: Variants are extracted by flood-filling the selected component from the base floor sheet, keeping neighboring tiles transparent. CombatBoardView loads them untrimmed so every tile retains the same isometric canvas and avoids neighbor-fragment warping.

notes.summary: CombatBoardView idle animation is data-driven per unit
notes.details: Definitions can override idle sheet columns, rows, order, and frame seconds while same-stem idle loading remains automatic. The default is 4x2 row-major at 0.10 seconds; Dust Acolyte uses 2x4 column-major at 0.20 seconds, covered by focused tests.

notes.summary: Combat board unit art honors per-definition art offsets
notes.details: CombatBoardView applies art_offset_x/y after fit and scale; adjust sprite centering in enemy or NPC data instead of changing global anchoring. Introduced for the Dust Acolyte alignment and covered by the enemy art-offset test.

notes.summary: Room moss lives in decorative metadata instead of terrain IDs
notes.details: RoomGenerator returns moss floor, wall, and pillar lists; CombatEngine and RunEngine carry them through room and combat state; CombatBoardView renders seeded overlays on stone floors and wall or pillar props. Passability and floor variants remain purely stone.

notes.summary: Boundary walls are hidden without hiding real doors
notes.details: With outer walls disabled, draw and hit-test order filter true boundary walls. Active exits and locked presentation doors remain door tiles, removing the old fake stone perimeter without breaking traversal.

notes.summary: Door placement uses explicit frame-scale constants
notes.details: DOOR_FRAME_WIDTH_SCALE, DOOR_FRAME_HEIGHT_SCALE, and DOOR_BASELINE_OFFSET_SCALE fit door.png on regular stone floor tiles. Tune those constants rather than changing the source asset or flip logic.

notes.summary: Door presentation uses the supplied isometric asset directly
notes.details: CombatBoardView draws door.png as a single overlay on regular stone floor tiles and flips it horizontally for the opposite diagonal. Generated skew variants are not used.

notes.summary: Valid cursor feedback is a dry mechanical click
notes.details: Keep the valid sound short and transient-led, with high-frequency contact texture and a close latch snap. Avoid a low body or ringing tail. The inert sound remains a longer dull dust-and-wood knock; preserve exact-once semantic classification and route both through the SFX bus.

notes.summary: Treasure rooms use the fixed corner-pillar layout
notes.details: RoomGenerator routes campfire and treasure rooms through the corner-pillar layout: stone floor with pillars at (2,2), (6,2), (2,6), and (6,6). This keeps center presentations clear.

notes.summary: Victory resolves missed equipment before clearing combat
notes.details: RunEngine.finish_combat marks every unclaimed equipment loot entry as missed and carries its id before clearing combat_state. RunScene may retain the pre-resolution victory snapshot only through the death dissolve animation, then uses the resolved snapshot for analytics and persistence. Grimoire discovery begins on collection, not visibility.

notes.summary: Progression synchronization distinguishes level-up purchases from same-level respec
notes.details: A newer profile revision that advances level supplies the post-purchase ember balance. A same-level respec revision preserves embers already held by the active run. Reconcile skill-event cursors before checkpoint persistence and baseline them when loading old saves.

notes.summary: Permanent skill benefits must remain monotonic and preserve player agency
notes.details: Qualitative skills should never make a previously legal action worse. Preservation effects such as keeping a Burn card or item require an explicit pre-arm choice; conditional bonus draws must not enter Fatigue solely because the permanent skill added the draw.

notes.summary: Earned deferred rewards survive skill-tree respec until one redemption
notes.details: Skill ownership gates acquisition of pending card, relic, or merchant benefits. Once earned, the pending value persists through respec and save repair, can be redeemed exactly once, and then clears.

notes.summary: Content-id renames require schema-gated recursive migration before subsystem repair
notes.details: Serialized runs can retain ids in loadouts, card piles, rewards, relics, merchant reservations, composite loot ids, discovery namespaces, nested intent state, terrain grids, checkpoints, and dictionary keys. For an older run_content_schema, apply exact replacements longest-first across the complete Variant graph before Grimoire or subsystem normalization, stamp the new schema, and atomically resave immediately on resume; persist migrated profile discovery ids separately.

notes.summary: Permanent progression saves are transactional and recoverable
notes.details: ProgressionStore writes normalized profile JSON to a validated temporary file, rotates a valid live profile to a short-lived backup, restores or retains that backup when replacement fails, and loads the backup when current JSON is missing or corrupt. Keep skill, ember, Moltshard, discovery, and run-history writes on this path.

notes.summary: GUI choice modals must not pre-consume their own button input
notes.details: Godot dispatches Node._input before Control GUI input. When SkillChoiceScrim is visible, consume only handled modal shortcuts such as Cancel; return without set_input_as_handled for Accept, mouse, and directional events so option Buttons receive them. On open, focus the first legal option and restore a live invoker or HUD fallback on close.

notes.summary: Skill-tree rules text must not resize the Character modal
notes.details: Keep variable-length status, requirements, unlock, and reason copy inside a bounded detail ScrollContainer. Pin the skill action and Cancel/Confirm footer outside that scroll, and size the graph plus detail widths to the 1280x720 body. Visual proof must assert the dialog combined minimum fits the viewport; checking only its assigned rect can miss children that push chrome offscreen.

notes.summary: Track banked-play consumption separately from total plays spent
notes.details: A banked play can pay for a card that grants a new ordinary play, so total capacity and cards_played_this_turn cannot reconstruct which slot remains. banked_play_spent_this_activation plus card_play_budget preserves the ordinary/banked split and resets each activation.

notes.summary: Keep skill-tree labels and rules outside the graph layer
notes.details: The tree uses compact stateful medallions, visible ports, and orthogonal connections inside protected graph space; full names, requirements, and effects live in the fixed detail pane so connections cannot be occluded. Direction is top-to-bottom rank, with node role and state communicated by shape plus color.

notes.summary: Progression analytics must stage durable intent before JSONL append
notes.details: For profile-owned rewards such as the first-boss Moltshard, persist the award and progression_analytics_outbox entry together before append. For combat skill triggers, copy every event newer than combat_skill_event_revision_staged into that same outbox and advance the staged cursor in the same committed combat checkpoint; the cursor means staged, never logged. Append only after the gameplay/outbox checkpoint succeeds, use stable run/combat idempotency keys, acknowledge separately after append, and carry terminal pending entries in the profile so crash, retry, and append-before-ack paths cannot lose or duplicate events. Analytics recovery must never bank held run Embers.

notes.summary: Combat skill card choices must guard previews and map displayed pile indices
notes.details: Manual ability activation is legal only from idle player-turn combat: no selected card, action-mode choice, drag, animation, pending Umbra commit, or existing skill-card selection. Otherwise a saved skill commit can be overwritten later by a stale card preview. Source-zone UI must also translate display order back to the engine's source order; discard piles render newest-first, so Encore buttons bind the reversed source index rather than their displayed index. Full-card hand choices use focusable wrappers with explicit Accept, Cancel, directional navigation, and focus restoration because CardWidget itself is intentionally mouse-only.

notes.summary: CardWidget interaction mode must survive tree entry
notes.details: Card selection wrappers are assembled before CardWidget enters the scene tree. Parent-side recursive mouse-filter changes made before add_child are not sufficient because CardWidget._ready runs afterward. CardWidget must derive mouse_filter from its configured interactive flag in both _ready and later configuration; callers that need nested tooltip hover must pass interactive=true explicitly, while wrapper-owned full-card choices pass false so the wrapper receives the click.

notes.summary: Card-selection prompts are positioned from the live hand boundary, and full-card discard choices require explicit focus frames.
notes.details: For in-hand skill targeting, lay the prompt out above hand_scroll after the hand is rebuilt instead of using fixed bottom offsets; fixed offsets covered card headers across aspect ratios. For discard-pile targeting, the transparent Button wrapper must draw normal/hover/pressed/focus frames and have explicit focus neighbors to the close action, because CardWidget itself does not own focus.

notes.summary: Player-facing horizontal scrollbars are banned, and skill trees must have no scrollbars on any sub-surface.
notes.details: Use fit-to-view and responsive reflow. The complete tree topology and selected ability rule/action must remain visible; compact layouts may rely on highlighted graph connections instead of redundant prerequisite prose. Enforced by spec/game_ui_rubric.md and tests/test_game_ui_rubric_inventory.py.

notes.summary: Every distinct player-facing icon-bearing concept must own a unique purpose-built icon.
notes.details: Abilities, relics, equipment, keywords, statuses, resources, and future icon-bearing families may reuse an icon only for the exact same concept. Different concepts may not share a resource path, byte-identical copy, recolor, badge overlay, or generic stand-in. Enforced by spec/icon_identity_policy.md and tests/test_icon_identity_policy.py.

notes.summary: Icon identity tests must audit consumers, not only asset inventories
notes.details: A unique registry can still be bypassed when RunScene or another consumer locally maps multiple named actions to one generic key, uses a procedural substitute, or falls back to a direct asset path. Keep card/enemy action types and grimoire topic keys centrally inventoried, allow only explicit exact-concept aliases, and assert the real consumers resolve through ActionIconLibrary.

notes.summary: Skill-tree interaction is click-driven, immediate, icon-led, and zone-preserving
notes.details: Pointer hover must never change skill selection, detail, focus, scroll, navigation, or connector geometry; only click/controller focus selects a node, and the no-scroll tree uses large medallions whose unique icons fill most of each face. Learning commits immediately without redundant success copy; whole-tree reset spends one Moltshard after one confirmation and refunds every earned point. Combat uses a labeled Abilities launcher with ready/owned counts and real owned-icon previews (compact below 1100 logical pixels), opening a fixed 800x492, ten-icons-per-page panel with complete two-line names and bounded descriptions. Only manual abilities show an action button. Hand discard and discard recovery select full cards in their source zones, then reuse normal discard/draw card-proxy motion and reduced-motion timing. Cache immutable authored order and connector obstacles to avoid first-open and learn stalls.

notes.summary: Board backdrops persist across every in-run board state
notes.details: Dungeon background art must use the same elevated near-orthographic camera as the isometric board: vertical pillars, floor axes aligned to the board's opposing diagonals (about +/-27 degrees), and architecture framing a quiet board-shaped center. Reject frontal one-point-perspective halls. Keep the backdrop dim, low-detail, and subordinate to gameplay, and show it whenever the in-run board is visible rather than gating it to combat. Every normal and transient board render submission must carry the backdrop transparency state, and that state must invalidate cached static rendering so an opaque grey/black fallback cannot linger.

notes.summary: Relic display templates resolve in natural units
notes.details: data/relics.json descriptions may use placeholders such as {value}, {0.value}, {action.amount}, and nested reward values. Player-facing copy must come from GameData.relic_def(), which resolves effect-derived values through the same 1x natural-unit action formatting used by combat; GameData.relics() remains raw data.

notes.summary: Combat uses natural 1x units with legacy save migration
notes.details: Cards, enemies, relic effects, terrain, pickups, healing, block, statuses, and fallback actions use the same natural integer values in data, combat, analytics, and UI. Player base max HP is 24. Run saves carry combat_units_schema=1; missing pre-natural saves with clear 10x evidence are converted once at load boundaries using survivor-preserving ceiling and cumulative round-half-up rules, while ambiguous conflicting saves are preserved. Defiance, not level-driven max-HP inflation, provides the permanent survivability clock.

notes.summary: Render unconfirmed combat previews from committed enemy durability plus projected overlays
notes.details: Targetless/self-centered AOE and earlier steps in multi-action cards can advance _preview_combat_state to zero HP or remove an enemy before Play Card confirmation. Feeding that projected state directly to CombatBoardView makes _build_visible_units drop the enemy. Keep projected position/status information, restore committed hp/block/stoneskin and missing committed enemies for display, and derive cumulative damage_preview from committed to projected state so empty bars and lethal markers remain visible.

notes.summary: Card-play relic draws must not redraw the card that triggered them or create Fatigue.
notes.details: When a finished card goes to discard, temporarily hold that card out while applying its relic rewards, restore it afterward, and safe-cap default relic draw rewards to the real draw+discard supply. Otherwise draw-trigger relics can self-loop or turn upside into accidental Fatigue damage.

notes.summary: Relic rarity is a conditional-power ladder, not a flat efficiency ladder.
notes.details: Common relics should be easy-to-trigger synergy nudges; rare and epic relics demand narrower or accumulated setup for larger engine payoffs; legendary relics should create run-defining turns only after mythic-level conditions. Avoid unconditional primary attack, health, block, or opening-resource boosts as the obvious picks.

notes.summary: Reward offers use a centered ruined raster banner and subordinate Recover
notes.details: Post-combat reward presentation uses one darkened stage stack: a reusable frayed raster instruction banner with restrained runtime text, exactly three centered card choices, then a compact Skip & Recover button with heal and HP projection. Relic rewards reuse the banner-and-centered-offer composition. Reward fixtures must default to the production three-card offer, never a hand-authored fourth card.

notes.summary: Player-facing buttons use code-native UiSkin construction
notes.details: Player-facing command buttons are built from UiSkin StyleBoxFlat states and ThemedButtonOrnament; the retired button_wood_gold bitmap families must not return. Button heights and variants remain shared UiSkin policy, while reward composition is governed separately by scripts/run_scene.gd.

notes.summary: Default UI visual QA to 1920x1080 at 100% UI scale
notes.details: Do not spend routine UI implementation time or proof budget on 720p, handheld, lower-resolution, or alternate-scale captures unless the user or task explicitly requests them; lower-resolution cleanup is intentionally deferred.

notes.summary: Combat popups begin close on the target's right side
notes.details: At the current 1920x1080/100% UI proof target, center every automatic combat popup 18 px to the right of the affected unit or terrain draw-rect center so overlap is expected and attribution stays immediate. Use the same rightward arc regardless of board position. Damage peaks at 60 px, short effects at 48 px, then both shrink along the continuous 0.96 s rise-and-fall arc; hold the peak through 0.32 progress to avoid stepped shrink. Compound effects keep 0.13 s pop-pop-pop staggering, while reduced motion remains a fixed local stack.

notes.summary: Relic event conditions use snapshots and off-turn plays carry forward
notes.details: For one card-play or status event, evaluate qualifying relic conditions from a shared post-action/post-intensity snapshot before applying same-event rewards, so acquisition order cannot create conditions. Relic card-play rewards earned off the player turn or while player_turn_ending is true accumulate in pending_relic_card_plays and transfer exactly once in prepare_next_player_turn.

notes.summary: Damage feedback commits combatant durability on its impact frame
notes.details: Diff enemy HP/Block/Stoneskin at player actions, card completion, turn end, enemy intensity, and enemy status steps. Status steps carry full post-step enemy/player/intensity snapshots so lethal Burn/Poison/Bleed can visibly sequence Ember Siphon and threshold discharges without state jumps. Reuse established impact decals/effects and hit flashes, skip paths that already present losses, and in reduced motion keep numbers/flash/decals static while suppressing shake and text rise/fade. Direct attacks render before_state through wind-up and after_state at impact. For non-attack actions with secondary enemy loss, render resolved primary state with enemy durability restored from before_state, then switch to after_state with secondary feedback. For move/blink trap impacts, retain the resolved destination and consumed trap but restore both player and enemy durability until _animate_player_trap_result. The shared durability helpers must not roll back intensity, position, statuses, or other resolved results.

notes.summary: Main-menu pointer handoff must not queue focus clearing behind mouse-down
notes.details: Clear keyboard focus synchronously on mouse motion only when no mouse button is held. A deferred clear from hover can run between a same-frame press and release and cancel native Button activation; preserve focus while button_mask is nonzero and defer the release-path clear until after activation.
